observation_summary: The command-line flag '--process_closure_primitives=false' is ignored, and closure primitives are processed even when explicitly disabled.
hypothesis: The code incorrectly sets the 'closurePass' option only when the flag is true, but fails to reset it to false when the flag is false, effectively leaving the default state (true) unchanged.
prediction: The fix will involve directly assigning the flag value to the option, ensuring that 'false' is correctly propagated to the compiler options.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows the removal of a conditional 'if' block that only set the option to true, replacing it with a direct assignment: 'options.closurePass = flags.process_closure_primitives;'. This confirms the root cause was an incorrect initialization/assignment logic.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic case of incorrect initialization logic where a boolean flag was not being correctly mapped to the configuration option. The fix replaces a conditional assignment with a direct assignment, which is the hallmark of an Assignment/Initialization defect.
evidence_used: The bug report explicitly states: 'Flag can't be set to false due to a missing "else" in the command-line parser.'
The fix diff shows: '- if (flags.process_closure_primitives) { options.closurePass = true; }' replaced by '+ options.closurePass = flags.process_closure_primitives;'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the original code used an 'if' statement, the root cause is not a missing validation check, but rather the failure to correctly assign the state of the flag to the configuration object.
